$comment: The one home of knobly's public API: every concept with its typed members, the kind lists, keywords, limits, patterns, error groups and free functions (spec/spec.md and spec/contract.md are canonical for behaviour; this file for the shapes). Types are written in the closed type grammar of spec/codegen.md section 2 and every name must resolve; spec/schema/api.schema.json checks the shape and tools/api/loader.py the rest. Names are spec names (lowercase words); each binding's spelling is derived from them by its casing rule (spec/binding-guide.md rule 1), never stored. Idiom that differs by language is a typed trait (spec/codegen.md section 3), never prose. History (removed names, settled disagreements) is in .claude/design/consumer-api/round15/schema-history.json.

layers.name: shared
layers.holds: positions, places, origins, diagnostics and the diagnostics sink, error groups, the kind lists

layers.name: io
layers.holds: the document source and writer ports, their adapters, and check lost updates (the one lost-update check every writer calls)

layers.name: written
layers.holds: the low level: processor, document graph, documents, statements, values, variables, the expansion and its expanded values with their readers, the extension port and the include extension (spec 5: an extension is pure, so it belongs to the layer that owns expansion)

layers.name: rendered
layers.holds: the rendered tree: render (graph), directives, arguments, addresses, diff

layer direction: A layer imports only the layers in its 'may import' list; nothing below the rendered layer imports, names or returns a rendered type (owner, 2026-10-29: "The low level shouldn't \"depend on\" the middle layer"). Going up a layer is the upper layer's free function: render (graph).

token kind.doc: the kinds of token, named as the grammar names them (WORD, STRING, SEMI, ...), in the order the grammar declares them

node kind.doc: the kinds of syntax tree node: the whole document, a directive, a block, a list, a slice, and a statement the parser could not read

statement kind.doc: the kinds of statement as written, one type each: a directive, an extension line, a set, snippet or use line, and a line that cannot be read

value kind.doc: the kinds of value, one type each: a word, a string, a list, a slice, an index, or a reference to a variable ($name); an expanded value is any of these but a reference

variable kind.doc: the kinds of variable, one type each: a set line's $name, a snippet's parameter, an override

step kind.doc: the kinds of expansion step: a variable replaced, a snippet used, files spliced in by an extension line

place kind.doc: where an origin's text is: in a file, or an override the program passed in

severity.doc: how much a diagnostic counts (spec 2.3): an error, or a warning, over which no operation throws, raises, fails or refuses; a program sees a warning only by reading a diagnostics list. A knobly code's letter gives it (E an error, W a warning); a program's own code is an error

unreadable reason.doc: why a statement could not be read: syntax (it holds a syntax error, or it is an extension line whose block holds one), expansion (a variable, snippet, use or set line could not be expanded), value (a value reached through a variable is not what its place takes, such as a slice bound that is not one integer), extension (an extension line failed: no file found, a read failed, or the extension refused it), unread (an extension line whose files are not read yet, E3007)

change kind.doc: the kinds of change between two renders

walk control.doc: what a walk's callback returns: skip passes over the item's block, stop ends the walk
walk control.rationale: the callback walk's idiom: TypeScript's walk takes a callback; Python's walk is a generator (break ends it, descend passes over a block), so the Python emitter omits this list

limits.name: nesting depth
limits.means: blocks and lists nested at most this deep

limits.name: expanded nesting depth
limits.means: blocks and lists nested at most this deep after expansion

limits.name: expansion depth
limits.means: use and extension lines nested at most this deep

limits.name: integer range
limits.means: integer words and slice or index bounds lie within plus or minus this (2^53-1)

reserved names.means: the language statements' names, written @set, @snippet and @use: no extension may take one. No directive name is reserved: a directive's name is a WORD, which never starts with @

variable name.means: a $name without its $, an override name, a variable rename

program code.means: <namespace>/<name>, a program's own diagnostic code: both parts non-empty, no whitespace (the Unicode White_Space set, written out); knobly's codes start with E or W

error groups.name: knobly error
error groups.raised when: never by itself: the base class of every expected-outcome class, so one except or catch clause catches every outcome the input or the outside world decides, and no program bug

error groups.name: diagnostic error
error groups.raised when: a reader is given a value of the wrong kind or spelling, or a program's error(...); carries one located diagnostic as 'diagnostic'

error groups.name: read error
error groups.raised when: load cannot resolve the root path to exactly one file, or cannot read it. No diagnostic and no code

error groups.name: bad text error
error groups.raised when: the text given to an edit, or an override's text, is not what that place takes, or the document after the edit would nest deeper than MAX_NESTING; 'diagnostics' are located in that text, in the binding's string unit, and its message is built from them

error groups.name: lost update error
error groups.raised when: a file the save would write changed since it was read or last saved: its current text differs from its saved text. Check lost updates raises it inside every writer, and save passes it on unchanged
error groups.doc: paths are only the conflicting files, in batch order

error groups.name: detached error
error groups.raised when: any member but kind of a detached handle is used

error groups.name: argument type error
error groups.raised when: an argument of the wrong type: anything but text where config text or a name is taken (an extension's name when the processor is made included), and to quote and text; a writer that is not a document writer; a render given something that is not a document graph (no callable expand); a key rule that returns anything but text or absent

error groups.name: misuse error
error groups.raised when: a bad argument value a program could have checked: every bad name (a variable or override name not matching the variable name pattern; a directive's new name, or an extension's name when the processor is made, that is not one word), a program code without '/', a reserved (set, snippet, use) or repeated extension name, a current list in check lost updates not as long as its files, and removing a slice's or index's name or its only bound

error groups.name: index out of range
error groups.raised when: an insert index outside a block; a token range outside a parse

argument type error message.rule: One helper per binding builds it (one home); every member that takes config text, quote, text, rename, set override, each load override and render call it before changing anything. Messages are for people (spec 2.3); the class and the member and parameter named are the contract.
argument type error message.got: the argument's type as the language names it (each emitter's sentence says how)
argument type error message.member: the member in the binding's casing, as the caller wrote it: set, replace with text, insert statements, add statements, insert before, insert after, set override, rename, quote, load, text, render
argument type error message.parameter: text; name for rename and for set override's name; overrides["<name>"] for a load override; raw for text; graph for render
argument type error message.other: a parameter that takes something other than text names what it takes instead of the language's word for a string

free functions.name: parse
free functions.doc: parses one text. Pure and total: it never raises for any input and reads no file; problems are reported in the syntax's diagnostics, and the tree still covers every token

free functions.name: span of
free functions.doc: the span of a token range. An empty range at index i is a zero-width span at the start of token i, or at the end of the text when i is the token count. Out of range when the range is outside 0 to the token count, or its start is after its end
free functions.rationale: spec 1, 'Where an operation lives', rule 4; stays a free function since milestone 1

free functions.name: text of
free functions.doc: the exact source text of a token range; for the root node, the whole input. Out of range as for span of
free functions.rationale: spec 1, 'Where an operation lives', rule 4; stays a free function since milestone 1

free functions.name: quote
free functions.doc: the text written as a knobly string, escapes included, as config text: 10.0.60.31 becomes "10.0.60.31", ready for an edit. The canonical string text an expanded value has

free functions.name: text
free functions.doc: raw as config text, unchanged and unchecked: the program's promise that raw is already knobly text (8080 as a value, [1, 2] as a list); the edit it is given checks it. With quote, the only maker of config text

free functions.name: render

errors.when: graph has no callable expand, before any other work

free functions.doc: the rendered tree of the graph's current texts and overrides: variables substituted, snippets used, extension files spliced in. Pure and synchronous: reads no file; an extension copy not read yet renders as an unreadable expansion with reason unread (its edge is in the graph's unread). Builds only on the graph's public expand, so it takes anything with the document graph's public members; given anything without a callable expand it fails with an argument type error before any other work
free functions.rationale: going up a layer is a free function of the upper layer (owner, 2026-10-29); exported only by the rendered layer's namespace (binding guide rule 9); the argument type check since milestone 5

free functions.name: format diagnostic
free functions.doc: the located diagnostic's text form (path:line:col: CODE: message), then the source line and a caret line under the span when graph holds the file (its current text), then one '  via <step>' line per step, innermost first. A line ends only at a line feed; columns and carets count the binding's string unit. Reads text only from graph; does no input or output
free functions.rationale: takes a document graph (a written type), so it belongs to the low level, not shared; was listed as shared in the first draft of this file

free functions.name: make processor

errors.when: an extension's name is not text
an extension's name is not one word, is a language statement's name (set, snippet, use), or is given twice

free functions.doc: makes a processor with its document source and extensions. An extension's name is written after @ (@include), so it must be one word (starting with a letter or one of _ . / * ?), and not a language statement's name (set, snippet, use) or one already taken

free functions.name: make diagnostics
free functions.doc: starts a diagnostics collection holding initial, in order (usually a render's diagnostics)

free functions.name: memory source
free functions.doc: a document source over texts held in memory, keyed by path. It reads the map it is given at each call, never a copy: what a memory writer (or the program) puts in that map, a later load or read sees. resolve joins the path spec to the directory of the parent path by POSIX rules ('/' separators, '.' and '..' removed, a leading '/' taken as is) and returns the path when it is a key; a glob in the last segment returns every key in that directory it matches. read of a path that is not a key fails. Pure: no input or output

free functions.name: memory writer
free functions.doc: a document writer into the map it is given (the one a memory source reads), so a save is seen by the next load. Each batch is all or nothing: it first calls check lost updates with each file's text in the map (empty when absent), and writes nothing when a file's text there differs from its saved text; then it sets every file's text

free functions.name: file source
free functions.doc: a document source over the local filesystem: read reads a path as given, as UTF-8; resolve joins a path spec to the directory of the parent path; a glob (* and ? in the last segment only) lists that directory and returns every matching file. A missing file or directory, or a path that is a directory, resolves to no paths (E3001); any other filesystem failure, such as permissions, fails (E3004)

free functions.name: file writer
free functions.doc: a document writer to the local filesystem, for one batch: it first calls check lost updates with each file's text on disk (a missing file holds no text), and writes nothing on a lost update; otherwise it writes each text, as UTF-8, to a temporary file beside its target (<name>.<random>.tmp), then renames each over its target in batch order. A failure while staging removes the temporaries and fails with nothing replaced; a failure while renaming can leave earlier files replaced, and removes the temporaries not yet renamed

free functions.name: fetch source
free functions.doc: a document source over fetch: resolve resolves a path spec as a URL against the parent path and returns it without fetching (globs resolve to no paths); read fetches the URL and fails on a response that is not a success

free functions.name: fetch writer
free functions.doc: a document writer that sends each file's text to its resolved path with fetch. First it GETs every file and calls check lost updates with the bodies (a 404 is no text), so a lost update fails before anything is sent; then one request per file, in batch order, with If-Match: <the GET's ETag> when the GET gave one: a 412 Precondition Failed is a lost update of that file. Without an ETag the window between the GET and the write stays open. It fails at the first failed request, so files sent before it stay written

free functions.name: include
free functions.doc: the include extension, which owns @include: its one value must be a quoted path or glob (E3005 otherwise, placed on the value), and the matching files are spliced in code-point order of resolved path. Its optional block of @set lines applies to the spliced files: @include "sink.conf" { @set $port 8080; }

free functions.name: check lost updates

params.name: current
params.doc: each file's text in the medium now, in the order of files; absent when there is none (read as empty text)

errors.when: a file's current text differs from its saved text; its paths are those files, in batch order
current is not as long as files, before any comparison

free functions.doc: the one lost-update check: raises a lost update error whose paths are the files whose current text differs from their saved text, in batch order. A current list not as long as files is a misuse error, raised before any comparison. Every writer calls it before it writes; a program's own writer should too

concepts.name: config text
concepts.doc: knobly text a program hands to an edit or an override, made only by quote or text; every edit's and override's text parameter takes it, so a plain string there is a type error the checker reports. Still the language's string at run time

concepts.name: source position

members.name: offset
members.doc: how many string units from the start of the text

members.name: line
members.doc: which line, counting from 0

members.name: column
members.doc: how many string units from the start of its line

concepts.doc: a point in one text: offset, line and column, each counting from 0. Offset and column count the binding's own string unit, so cutting the program's string at a position gives the right text. A line ends after each line feed (a carriage return and line feed end one line); a lone carriage return does not end a line

concepts.name: source span

members.name: start
members.doc: the first position in the range

members.name: end
members.doc: the position just after the range; equal to start for an empty range

concepts.doc: a half-open range [start, end) of one text; start is never after end

concepts.name: place

members.name: kind
members.doc: always 'file': it tells a place from an override

members.name: resolved path
members.doc: the file's identity, as the document source resolved it

members.name: span
members.doc: the range within that file's text

members.name: people form
members.doc: the text path:line:col at the span's start, counting from 1, in the binding's string unit: main.conf:4:5. Every located thing's text form, and format diagnostic, build on it

concepts.doc: a range of one file's text: where a directive, a value, a step or a problem is written

concepts.name: override

members.name: kind
members.doc: always 'override': it tells an override from a place

members.name: variable
members.doc: the variable's name, without $

members.name: people form
members.doc: the text override <variable>, without $: override port

concepts.doc: a value the program passed in at load or with set override, written in no file: an origin's place when the text came from one

concepts.name: step

members.name: kind
members.doc: which expansion: variable, use or extension

members.name: name
members.doc: the variable without $, the snippet's name, or the extension's name without @ (include)

members.name: place
members.doc: where the step is written: the $name token, the @use of the use line, or the extension line's @name

members.name: people form
members.doc: the text <kind> <name> at <place>: variable pixels at main.conf:4:15

concepts.doc: one expansion a directive or value went through to reach where it is read: variable ($pixels replaced by its value), use (a snippet's body spliced in) or extension (files spliced in by an extension line)

concepts.name: origin

members.name: place
members.doc: where the text is written: a file place, or an override

members.name: via
members.doc: the steps that brought it here, innermost first; empty when the text is read where it is written

concepts.doc: where a value came from: its place (a file place, or an override) and the steps that brought it to where it is read. For a value from a variable, place is the value in its set line (or the override) and the first step is the $name that used it

concepts.name: directive origin

members.name: place
members.doc: where it is written

members.name: via
members.doc: the steps that brought this copy here, innermost first; empty when it is read where it is written

concepts.doc: an origin whose place is always a file place: where a directive's name or a statement is written, and the steps that brought this copy there

concepts.name: diagnostic

members.name: code
members.doc: which problem

members.name: severity
members.doc: the code's severity (spec 2.3): always error, since parse finds no warning

members.name: message
members.doc: the problem in words, for people

members.name: span
members.doc: where in the text the problem is

members.name: people form
members.doc: the text line:col: CODE: message, counting from 1, at the span's start

concepts.doc: one problem the syntax layer found in one text. Only the code and the span are part of the contract: the message is for people and may differ between bindings

concepts.name: program code
concepts.doc: a program's own diagnostic code, '<namespace>/<name>' (the program code pattern)
concepts.rationale: TypeScript checks the '/' in the type (the template, '${string}/${string}'); Python has no such type, so it is text there, checked at run time

concepts.name: located diagnostic

members.name: code
members.doc: a diagnostic code, or the program's own program code (rasl/unknown-node)

members.name: severity
members.doc: the code's severity (spec 2.3): error, or warning for a W code (W3005); a program's own code is always an error

members.name: message
members.doc: the problem in words, for people

members.name: place
members.doc: the file place it is reported at

members.name: via
members.doc: the steps that brought the text there, innermost first

members.name: people form
members.doc: the text path:line:col: CODE: message, the first line of format diagnostic

concepts.doc: one problem of a load, knobly's or a program's, always at a place in a file. A problem caused by an override is placed at the $name that used it, and its message names the variable

concepts.name: locatable

members.name: error
members.doc: a diagnostic error placed on this thing, for the program to raise or report: it is returned, not raised. Its diagnostic carries the message and the program's code, which must hold '/'

concepts.doc: anything a program can place a problem on: a directive, an expanded value, the render

concepts.name: diagnostics

members.name: add
members.doc: appends one located diagnostic

members.name: report
members.doc: appends the diagnostic that the error of at, given this message and code, would carry: a program's own problem placed on a rendered tree, a directive or an expanded value. The code must hold '/' (rasl/unknown-node)

members.name: count
members.doc: how many diagnostics it holds, warnings included

members.name: iterate
members.doc: every diagnostic it holds

members.name: collect
members.doc: runs the callback read and returns what it returns; when read raises an error carrying one diagnostic (a reader's error), it records that diagnostic and returns absent instead; any other error passes through
members.rationale: Python's context manager is an allowed difference (binding guide section 3); the doc is spec 7.7's collect row

concepts.doc: the one place problems collect: a program starts it with a render's diagnostics, reports its own problems into it, and runs reads through collect so a reader's diagnostic error is recorded instead of ending the program

concepts.name: block

members.name: iterate
members.doc: its items, as they are when iteration starts, so an edit while iterating never skips or repeats one

members.name: count
members.doc: how many items it holds

members.name: at
members.doc: the item at an index, counting from 0

members.name: directives
members.doc: its directives, only those with that name when a name is given. A written block lists written directives only, never extension lines

members.name: walk
members.order: depth first, written order; the block's owner is not included
members.doc: every item in this block and in the blocks its items hold, at any depth, depth-first: an item, then everything in its block, then its next sibling. The caller can skip an item's block or stop early

concepts.doc: the one block shape of every layer: iterated and indexed in order, its directives by name, and a depth-first walk over its items at any depth. The written block holds statements, the expansion block directive expansions, the rendered block directives
concepts.rationale: binding guide rule 5; owner, 2026-10-29: "Yes, rename now"

concepts.name: token range

members.name: start
members.doc: the index of the first token

members.name: end
members.doc: the index just after the last token; equal to start for an empty range

concepts.doc: a half-open range of token indices; a node is one

concepts.name: token

members.name: kind
members.doc: which token, a name from the grammar (WORD, STRING, SEMI, ...)

members.name: text
members.doc: its exact source text, never empty

members.name: span
members.doc: where it is in the text

concepts.doc: one token of a parse: its kind, exact text and span. The tokens of one parse are contiguous and in source order, none is empty, and their texts joined are the input exactly

concepts.name: node

members.name: kind
members.doc: document, directive, block, list, slice or error

members.name: children
members.doc: its child nodes, in source order, inside its range and not overlapping; an error node has none

concepts.doc: one node of the syntax tree: its kind, its token range and its children. Tokens no child covers belong to the node itself

concepts.name: syntax

members.name: tokens
members.doc: every token, in source order

members.name: root
members.doc: the document node over every token

members.name: diagnostics
members.doc: the syntax problems, in the order the parser reaches them; empty exactly when the text is valid

concepts.doc: the lossless syntax tree of one text: every token, the root node over them, and the problems found. Joining the tokens' texts gives the input back exactly

concepts.name: load context

members.name: parent path
members.doc: the resolved path of the file holding the extension line; empty when the root path itself is resolved

concepts.doc: what a document source is told when it resolves a path spec

concepts.name: document source

members.name: resolve
members.doc: the resolved paths a path spec names (a path, or a glob with * and ? in its last segment), in any order: the core sorts them. Empty means not found (E3001); a failure becomes E3004 at the extension line

members.name: read
members.doc: the text of one resolved file. A failure becomes E3004 at the extension line, or, for the root file, makes load fail with a read error. A load reads each resolved path at most once

concepts.doc: where files come from: the program's port that resolves path specs and reads files, so the core does no input or output

concepts.name: file write

members.name: resolved path
members.doc: the file to write

members.name: text
members.doc: what to write

members.name: saved text
members.doc: the document's last-read or last-saved text: compared with what the medium holds now, to find a lost update

concepts.doc: one file of the batch a document writer is handed

concepts.name: document writer

members.name: write
members.doc: commits one batch together. It first calls check lost updates with each file's text in the medium now, writing nothing when that raises; a failure while staging means nothing was committed

concepts.doc: where files go: the program's port that commits one batch of files together

concepts.name: fetch writer options

members.name: method
members.doc: the HTTP method; default PUT

members.name: content type
members.doc: the Content-Type header; default text/plain

concepts.doc: the fetch writer's options

concepts.name: platform fetch
concepts.doc: the platform's fetch, passed in so the core reaches no global

concepts.name: extension

members.name: directive
members.doc: the name it owns, without @: include. A line uses it when written @include; making the processor refuses a reserved (set, snippet, use), repeated, or malformed (not one word) name

members.name: specs
members.doc: the specs for one use, in splice order. Raise a diagnostic error for a located failure; any other failure, or a result that is not a list of texts, becomes E3006 at the directive's name

concepts.doc: a plug-in that owns one directive name and turns each line written with it (@include) into path specs of files to splice in its place. It is pure: the load resolves, reads and splices the files

concepts.name: extension use

members.name: values
members.doc: the line's values, expanded, with their links

members.name: origin
members.doc: where the line's name is written, and the steps that brought this copy there

concepts.doc: one line written with an extension's name, as the extension sees it

concepts.name: load options

members.name: overrides
members.doc: the overrides by name, without $, each as config text, in order; each wins over every set line of its name

concepts.doc: the options load takes

concepts.name: processor options

members.name: source
members.doc: the document source every file is read through

members.name: extensions
members.doc: the extensions to turn on; none when left out

concepts.doc: what a processor is made with

concepts.name: processor

members.name: load

errors.when: an override's name does not match the variable name pattern, before any file is read
path is not text, or an override's text is not config text

members.doc: reads the root file at path (resolved through the source as an included file's path spec is, so the root has one path in the graph) and every file its extension lines name, once each, repeating until nothing new is named, and returns the document graph. Never fails for anything in the text: those problems are diagnostics. Each override is by name without $, as config text, and is checked as set override checks it, in order, before any file is read. The read error's paths hold the root path

concepts.doc: what loads documents: made with a document source and extensions, it loads any number of times; load is its only operation

concepts.name: document graph

members.name: root
members.doc: the root document

members.name: documents
members.doc: every document read, by resolved path: root first, then in first-read order; never shrinks

members.name: overrides
members.doc: the overrides by name, without $, each the config text the program gave, in order; never saved. Change them with set override

members.name: set override

errors.when: name is not text, or text is not config text or absent
name does not match the variable name pattern

members.doc: adds, changes or (given absent) removes one override without a reload. The name must be letters, digits and _; the text must be one or more values without a $name, else a bad text error located in that text. A changed name keeps its place; a new one goes last

members.name: read
members.doc: resolves and reads what unread names, through the graph's document source, repeating until nothing new is named; keeps every text and every failure it already had. Returns the resolved paths this call read

members.name: save

errors.when: the writer fails with one; it passes through unchanged

members.doc: hands every document whose text differs from its saved text to writer in one batch; with none, the writer is not called. When the writer returns, each written document's saved text becomes the text it was given (an edit made while the writer ran stays unsaved); when it fails, nothing changes: a lost update error passes through as it is, and any other failure becomes a save error whose paths are the batch's and whose cause is that failure. Returns the resolved paths handed over

members.name: edges
members.doc: every copy of every extension line

members.name: unread
members.doc: the edges naming a path spec not resolved or a file not read yet; each such copy expands to an unreadable expansion with reason unread, and E3007 in diagnostics

members.name: variables
members.order: set and parameters in document order, then overrides in overrides order
members.doc: every variable, only those with that name when a name is given

members.name: diagnostics
members.doc: the one list: each document's syntax diagnostics (documents in order), then every problem the low level finds, in walk order, render codes and warnings included (a program tells them apart by severity). The expansion's and the render's diagnostics are this same list

members.name: expand
members.doc: the graph's current texts and overrides after expansion: every copy of every directive as read, its values linked to the written text, and what could not be read. What render builds the rendered tree from. A snapshot (make a new one after any change); pure: reads no file

concepts.doc: the files one load read, and the overrides the program passed in. It keeps the document source and extensions it was loaded with, so it reads and saves itself (the core still does no input or output: the source and the writer do)
concepts.rationale: has no render member and names no rendered type (owner, 2026-10-29)

concepts.name: document

members.name: resolved path
members.doc: its identity: the path the document source resolved

members.name: saved text
members.doc: the text as read, or as last handed to a writer that succeeded

members.name: text
members.doc: the text now; differs from saved text exactly when there are unsaved changes

members.name: syntax
members.doc: the syntax tree of its text now

members.name: block
